Sam: Heads-up — saw a 3–5x p50 CPU bump on ingress parsing during the streaming load test this morning, started ~09:10UTC. stackprof + flame looks host-side not decode path.
Priya: link? did it correlate with a model change or infra deploy? :thinking:
Sam: infra deploy at 09:05 — but only control-plane. no model or runtime change. attaching quick perf dump below.
Sam: ```
# top-ish diff from perf trace (host process)
30%  parse_frame::read_chunks
18%  socket_writev
12%  header_parsing::http2_settings
8%   kv_cache::get_prefix
6%   batch_window::recompute
```
Diego: hm writev dominance suggests more fragmentation — maybe chunker isn't coalescing streaming frames. any change in client-side chunk size?
Sam: clients steady. load generator reproduces locally if I run with multiplex 200 conns. patching server to force larger writev coalescing drops cost ~40%.
Nina: nice. does that affect latency tail?
Sam: p95 improved from 320ms -> 220ms on host framing, total p95 for token generation unchanged (GPU-bound), so this is pure host-side overhead saved.
Priya: can we route around by tweaking batching heuristics? if batcher is emitting smaller payloads, host churn goes up.
Diego: I think two orthogonal issues: 1) framing -> IO syscalls, 2) kernel selection path hit due to variable seq lengths in streaming. When host spends more time slicing requests it ends up picking fallback kernels (scalar) for small windows.
Sam: exact. profile shows fallback_kernels counter up ~x6 during the spike.
Sam: ```
runtime.metrics: {fallback_kernels: 612, fast_kernels: 88, kv_hit_rate: 0.73}
```
Priya: kv hit rate drop to .73 is suspicious. was there a spike in prefix churn?
Sam: yes, small prompts with lots of unique prefixes from the generator. kv misses cause extra parsing and recompute.
Nina: two quick ideas: 1) server-side coalesce writev with short timer jitter at ingress to reduce syscall flood, 2) add a temporary kernel-hint header so that routing can prefer fast kernels for <=32 steps windows while we stabilize cache.
Diego: second option needs an API change but we can prototype with an internal header: `x-rw-kernel-hint: prefer-vector` and test. I'll sketch a small patch to gateway to set hint when (seq_len <= 32 && batch_size >= 4).
Sam: before rolling, can we simulate with loadgen? I ran a microtest: forcing coalesce via `SO_SNDBUF=256k` + a 3ms coalesce timer cut writev syscalls by 70% and lowered CPU by ~35%.
Priya: good data. what about HTTP/2 vs gRPC path differences?
Sam: gRPC/HTTP2 path had slightly better coalesce because of internal buffering; pure http1 streaming suffered worst. Our infra-bot also notes a deploy to the HTTP1 proxy at 09:04.
InfraBot: deploy/gateway-proxy v2.14.1 completed by deploy-bot at 2026-03-18T09:05:12Z (sha:abc123). No rollback.
Nina: actionable plan:
- short term: enable writev coalescing in HTTP1 proxy (3ms timer, sndbuf bump) gated behind feature flag.
- medium: add `x-rw-kernel-hint` header from gateway to runtime; runtime will prefer vectorized kernels for flagged flows.
- long: tune batching window heuristics to account for prefix churn and introduce sticky KV shards per client to reduce invalidations.
Diego: I'll prototype kernel-hint patch and a tiny opt-in flag in gateway. Sam can run loadgen tests.
Sam: will run loadgen + perf traces. will also produce a diff of syscall counts and fallback_kernels metrics.
Priya: assign follow-ups: Diego -> kernel-hint POC (PR by EOD), Nina -> coalesce flag rollout plan, Sam -> perf artifacts and validation matrix.
Sam: thanks. I'll paste a short reproduction script here shortly.
Sam: ```bash
# reproduce locally
make dev-loadgen && ./loadgen --conns 200 --prompts small-prefixes.txt --http1-streaming --rps 800
# then collect perf
perf record -F 99 -g -p $(pidof redwood-runtime) -- sleep 60 && perf script > /tmp/trace.stacks
```
Priya: perfect. keep thread updated. :thumbsup:
